QASHANI:92:13-17/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:92:13-17/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:92:13-17/r4.claim: Only the most wretched, lacking readiness and sharing in shirk, enters it: the one who denies God and turns away stubbornly.
QASHANI:92:13-17/r4.anchor: العديم الاستعداد، الخبيث الجوهر، المشرك بالله في المواقف الأربعة

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r7.claim: Verses 15–21 explain the traits of those cast into Hell and those shielded from it, together with their reward.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r7.anchor: An explanation of the character of people who will be thrown into Hell and those who will be shielded from it

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r3.claim: The warning addresses Quraysh: persistent deniers of truth face the blazing fire, while those who spend to attain purity are protected from it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r3.anchor: people who spend their wealth to attain purity will be shielded from this fire.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r4.claim: The contrast is between rejecters of God’s Messengers and believers, not degrees of wickedness or piety; conclusive warning leaves Messenger-rejecters no legitimate excuse, making them the most wretched.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r4.anchor: less pious and the more pious

FARRA:v3p272/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p272/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p272/r3.claim: Kadhdhaba and turned away need not mean explicit denial; failure to obey can be called denial, as when a fighter retreats.
FARRA:v3p272/r3.anchor: وقوله عز وجل: الذي كذب وتولى (16) . لم يكن كذب برد ظاهر، ولكنه قصر عما أمر به من الطاعة،

FARRA:v3p272/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p272/r4.speaker: أبو ثروان
FARRA:v3p272/r4.claim: Abū Tharwān says Banū Numayr have no falsehood: they fight truthfully and do not retreat.
FARRA:v3p272/r4.anchor: قال الفراء: وسمعت أبا ثروان يقول: إن بني نمير ليس لجدهم مكذوبة.

FARRA:v3p272/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p272/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p272/r5.claim: Likewise, lā kādhibata means the Hour's occurrence is certain and cannot be denied.
FARRA:v3p272/r5.anchor: ليس لوقعتها كاذبة » يقول: هي حق.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r6.claim: The warning to Mecca is of a flaming fire; only the wretched, who denied the Messenger and turned from faith, enters it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r6.anchor: {فأنذرتكم} يا أهل مكة، {نارا تلظى لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى} أي: تتلظى، يعني تتوقد وتتوهج

BAYDAWI-FULL:92:13-19/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:13-19/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:13-19/r4.claim: The unbeliever denied the truth and turned away from obedience.
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:13-19/r4.anchor: { الذى كذب وتولى } أي كذب الحق وأعرض عن الطاعة

BINTSHATI:v2p115/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p115/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p115/r1.claim: Because al-ashqa is definite and unqualified, it denotes the absolutely most wretched, without comparison among kinds of wretched people.
BINTSHATI:v2p115/r1.anchor: فيهما يطلق "الأشقى" من كل قيد، فلا مجال لمفاضلة بين أي شقي

BINTSHATI:v2p115/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p115/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p115/r2.claim: The wretched person in this passage is the one who denies and turns away.
BINTSHATI:v2p115/r2.anchor: والأشقى في آية الليل: {الذي كذب وتولى}

BINTSHATI:v2p115/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p115/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p115/r3.claim: Arabic kadhb means a statement failing to match reality or what is inward, and can also mean disappointing an expectation.
BINTSHATI:v2p115/r3.anchor: الكذب في العربية، عدم مطابقة القول للواقع أو لما في الضمير

BINTSHATI:v2p115/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p115/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p115/r4.claim: Quranic takdhib is religious denial of God, signs, blessings, revelations, messengers, meeting God, or the Last Day.
BINTSHATI:v2p115/r4.anchor: ولا يأتي التكذيب في الاستعمال القرآني، إلا بالمعنى الديني في التكذيب بالله وآياته

BINTSHATI:v2p115/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p115/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p115/r5.claim: Tawalla means turning away and retreating; the Quran pairs it with disbelief and denial in parallel warnings.
BINTSHATI:v2p115/r5.anchor: والتولى: الإعراض والإدبار. وقد جاء قريناً للكفر والتكذيب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r2.claim: Only the most wretched, meaning the unbeliever, undergoes the fire permanently; a sinful believer may enter but will not remain there.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r2.anchor: فإن الفاسق وإن دخلها لا يكون ذلك له على طريق اللزوم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r3.claim: The one who lied and turned away corrupted his knowing faculty by arrogantly rejecting truth and refusing to give wealth for self-purification.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r3.anchor: الذي كذب } أي أفسد قوته العلمية بأن أعرض عن الحق تكبرا وعنادا فلم يؤت ماله لزكاة نفسه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r6.claim: The passage uses reciprocal omission: mentioning denial first implies its opposite later, while mentioning giving later implies its opposite was omitted first.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r6.anchor: والآية من الاحتباك : ذكر التكذيب أولا دليلا على حذف ضده ثانيا

NAHHAS:v5p243/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p243/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p243/r7.claim: The word is glossed as falling short, supported by the Arab expression that someone carried on against another and did not fall short.
NAHHAS:v5p243/r7.anchor: أي قصر أخذه من قول العرب حمل فلان على فلان فما

DURR-FULL:v8p536/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r7.claim: The Prophet said all would enter Paradise except those who refuse; when asked who refuses, he recited ‘the one who denied and turned away.’
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r7.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن أبي هريرة

DURR-FULL:v8p536/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r8.speaker: أبو أمامة
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r8.claim: He said everyone in the community enters Paradise except one who rebels against God like a bad camel against its owner, citing the description of the wretched denier.
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r8.anchor: وأخرج سعيد بن منصور وابن أبي حاتم وابن المنذر والطبراني وابن مردويه عن أبي أمامة

DURR-FULL:v8p536/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r9.speaker: أبو أمامة الباهلي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r9.claim: The Prophet said everyone enters Paradise except one who bolts from God as a camel bolts from its owner.
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r9.anchor: وأخرج أحمد والحاكم عن أبي أمامة الباهلي

DURR-FULL:v8p536/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r10.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r10.claim: The Prophet said everyone enters Paradise except the one who refuses; whoever obeys him enters, and whoever disobeys has refused.
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r10.anchor: وأخرج أحمد والبخاري عن أبي هريرة

DURR-FULL:v8p536/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r11.speaker: أبو أمامة
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r11.claim: The Prophet said only the wretched enter the Fire; the wretched are those who neither obey God nor refrain from disobedience.
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r11.anchor: وأخرج أحمد وابن مردويه عن أبي أمامة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r3.claim: The clause excluding all but the most wretched from this particular Fire is a second descriptor or a circumstantial clause; this is the Fire prepared for disbelievers, as in al-Baqara, and the next verse confirms it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r3.anchor: وهذه نار خاصة أعدت للكافرين فهي التي في قوله : { فاتقوا النار التي وقودها الناس والحجارة أعدت للكافرين } ( البقرة : 24 ) والقرينة على ذلك قوله : { وسيجنبها الأتقى } الآية .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق الزجاج
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj says this verse prompted the Murjiʾa to claim that only unbelievers enter Hell; Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects the generalization because this is one specific Fire and Hell has levels, including the lowest for hypocrites.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r4.anchor: وذكر القرطبي أن أبا إسحاق الزجاج قال : هذه الآية التي من أجلها قال أهل الإرجاء بالإرجاء فزعموا : أن لا يدخل النار إلا كافر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r5.claim: The most wretched are explicitly identified as those who denied the Messenger and turned away from the Quran; in the early Islamic audience this described the disbelievers, while the most God-fearing are named to complete the contrast.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r5.anchor: وقد أتبع { الأشقى } بصفة { الذي كذب وتولى } لزيادة التنصيص على أنهم المقصود بذلك فإنهم يعلمون أنهم كذبوا الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم وتولوا

JISHUMI:v10p7447/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r2.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r2.claim: He gives three explanations of “none enters it but the most wretched”: only one matching the stated traits approaches it; the Fire is named for its majority and intended occupants; or “only” signals the most deserving, without excluding others.
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r2.anchor: ذكر هذه الوجوه الثلاثة أبو مسلم

JISHUMI:v10p7447/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r3.claim: The exclusionary reading cannot mean that no sinful person enters Hell: that would contradict consensus, encourage or permit sin, and conflict with the threat against the miser and sinner.
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r3.anchor: لوجب القطع على أن الفاسق لا يدخل النار، وفيه خلاف الإجماع، وإغراء بالمعاصي

JISHUMI:v10p7447/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r4.claim: Another explanation supplies an ellipsis: “the most wretched, and whoever is like him among the sinners.”
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r4.anchor: كأنه قيل: الأشقى، ومن جرى مجراه من العصاة

JISHUMI:v10p7447/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r5.claim: A further view says some disbelievers enter the Fire without having committed each specified act of denial, miserliness, and turning away; the author says the first explanation is best.
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r5.anchor: أن من الكفار من يدخلها، وإن لم يكذب، ولم يبخل، ولم يتول

JISHUMI:v10p7447/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r6.claim: He prefers the first of the explanations of who enters the Fire.

MUQATIL:92:16-21/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:92:16-21/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:92:16-21/r1.claim: The one who denies the Quran and turns from faith is among those liable to the Fire.
MUQATIL:92:16-21/r1.anchor: { الذي كذب وتولى } [آية: 16] الذين كذبوا بالقرآن وتولى يعني أعرض عن الإيمان

STUDYQURAN:92:15/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r1.speaker: several commentators
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r1.claim: Commentators tell of a Medinan palm owner who snatched fallen dates from a poor family's children and refused the Prophet's offer of a Paradise palm; another man paid forty palms, donated the tree, and the Prophet gave it to the family. The refusal maps to vv. 15–16, the gift to vv. 18–21.
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r1.anchor: Several commentators say that the whole of this sūrah was revealed in reference to a Muslim of Madinah who had a palm tree

STUDYQURAN:92:15/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r2.claim: If this is an early Makkan sūrah, the palm-tree story likely is not its occasion; the verses instead generally condemn those who rejected Muhammad as prophet.
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r2.anchor: If, however, this is an early Makkan sūrah, as some maintain

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.claim: The sura develops two antitheses: behavior and recompense for the saved and damned, first in verses 5–13 and then in verses 14–21.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.anchor: Es folgen zwei Antithesen (V. 5–13 und V. 14–21), welche die Verhaltensweisen und Jenseitsschicksale von Seligen und Verdammten miteinander kontrastieren

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.claim: The final stanza reverses the earlier order of saved and damned; the outer blessed sections are linked by ittaqā in verse 5 and ʾatqā in verse 17.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.anchor: Zum einen wird die Reihenfolge Seliger – Verdammter (V. 5–7 und V. 8–11) jetzt invertiert (V. 14–16 Verdammter, V. 17–20 Seliger)

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.claim: The stanza halves mirror one another: earlier behavior lists precede reward or warning, while the final warning and promise precede each group's worldly conduct.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.anchor: In V. 5–7 und V. 8–11 ging zunächst ein Tugend- bzw. Lasterkatalog voraus, auf den dann jeweils ein Drohwort bzw. eine Verheißung folgten

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r3.claim: The second antithesis concretizes the first: verse 14 resolves the enigmatic threat of verse 10 as the image of blazing Hell.

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r4.claim: This movement from riddle to shocking disclosure resembles the teaching question and explicit Hell image in 104:4–7 and the eschatological resolution in 102:3–8.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r4.anchor: Eine analoge Sequenz aus Enigma und eschatologischer Auflösung liegt Q 102:3–8 zu Grunde

ELMALILI:92:12-21/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r6.claim: The most wretched is the disbeliever, defined as one who denies God's guidance and turns away from the truth.
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r6.anchor: “Eşkā”dan murad kâfir olduğu anlatılmak için şununla beyan ve tefsir olunmuştur

ELMALILI:92:12-21/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r7.claim: A sinner who turns away without denying is wretched but not the most wretched; even if he enters the Fire, he does not remain there.
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r7.anchor: Tekzib etmeksizin i‘râz eden fâsık ise en şakī değil şakīdir, o ateşe girerse de yaslanıp kalmaz.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.claim: Others say verses 5–19 were revealed about Abu Bakr; regardless of a specific occasion, the message and rulings are general.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.anchor: bazıları ise 5-19. âyetlerin (bk. Elmalılı, VIII, 5881), müşriklerin işkence ettiği köleleri satın alıp âzat ederek hürriyetlerine kavuşturan Hz. Ebû Bekir hakkında indiğini söylemişlerdir. Âyetler böyle bir özel olay üzerine gelmiş olsa da, hükümleri ve mesajları geneldir

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3441#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3441#3/r1.speaker: أبو أمامة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3441#3/r1.claim: Abu Umama says no one of this community enters Hell except one who flees from God; the one who enters is the most wretched, who denied Muhammad's message and turned away from him.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3441#3/r1.anchor: عن أبي امامة قال : لا يبقى أحد من هذه الامة الا ادخله الله الجنة الا من شرد علي الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p151#5/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p151#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p151#5/r1.claim: The person denied the Messenger and turned away from faith; al-ashqā here means al-shaqī, since Arabic uses the elative form for an active participle, as Ṭarafa's verse illustrates.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p151#5/r1.anchor: الذي كذب الرسول ﴿ وتولى ﴾ عن الإيمان قال أبو عبيدة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p151#5/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p151#5/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p151#5/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj rejects the Murjiʾa inference that only unbelievers enter Hell: this is one particular Fire, and Hell has ranks; otherwise 4:48 would have no point.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p151#5/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج وهذه الآية التي من أجلها زعم أهل الإرجاء أنه لا يدخل النار إلا كافر

MAJAZ:v2p301/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p301/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p301/r2.claim: Arabic can use the elative pattern afʿal where an active participle fāʿil is meant; Ṭarafa’s awḥad illustrates this.
MAJAZ:v2p301/r2.anchor: «لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى» (16) والعرب تضع «أفعل» فى موضع «فاعل» قال طرفة: تمنى رجال أن أموت وإن أمت ... فتلك سبيل لست فيها بأوحد

MUJAHID:v2p765#4/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p765#4/r1.speaker: أبو أمامة
MUJAHID:v2p765#4/r1.claim: Abu Umama says the one who denied and turned away rejected what Muhammad brought and turned away from him.
MUJAHID:v2p765#4/r1.anchor: عن أبي أمامة في قوله ﴿ الذي كذب وتولى ﴾ يقول كذب بما جاء به محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وتولى عنه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p344/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p344/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p344/r1.claim: Only the most wretched unbeliever, who denied the messengers and turned away from faith, enters the Fire eternally.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p344/r1.anchor: ﴿ لا يصلاها ﴾ لا يدخلها للخلود فيها ﴿ إلا الأشقى الذي كذب وتولى ﴾

QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r6.claim: The one who denied is the one who denied Muhammad and turned away from faith.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r6.anchor: { الذي كذب } نبي الله محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم. { وتولى } أي أعرض عن الإيمان

QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r7.speaker: مكحول، أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r7.claim: Makhul transmits from Abu Hurayra that everyone enters Paradise except one who refuses; the refuser denied and turned away.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r7.anchor: وروى مكحول عن أبي هريرة قال: كل يدخل الجنة إلا من أباها

QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r11.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r11.claim: Qatada says the person denied God’s Book and turned away from obeying Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r11.anchor: وقال قتادة: كذب بكتاب الله، وتولى عن طاعة الله

QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r12.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r12.claim: Al-Farra says denial need not be explicit: falling short of commanded obedience counts as denial, like a fighter who turns back; “no falsehood” at 56:2 means the event is true.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r12.anchor: وقال الفراء: لم يكن كذب برد ظاهر، ولكنه قصر عما أمر به من الطاعة فجعل تكذيبا

QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r13.speaker: أبو ثروان
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r13.claim: Al-Farra quotes Abu Tharwan: Banu Numayr’s ancestor has no falsehood, meaning they fight and do not turn back.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r13.anchor: قال: وسمعت أبا ثروان يقول: إن بني نمير ليس لجدهم مكذوبة

QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r14.claim: The same figurative use occurs at 56:2, where “no lying” means the event is true.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r14.anchor:
وكذلك قوله جل ثناؤه:
ليس لوقعتها كاذبة
[الواقعة: 2] يقول هي حق

QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r15.speaker: أبو إسحاق الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r15.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the Murjiites wrongly infer that only unbelievers enter Hell: this names one particular fire, while Hell has levels and other promised punishments remain possible.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r15.anchor: أبا إسحاق الزجاج يقول: هذه الآية التي من أجلها قال أهل الإرجاء بالإرجاء، فزعموا أنه لا يدخل النار إلا كافر

QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16#2/r1.claim: If every non-polytheist were exempt from punishment, the promise to forgive lesser sins “for whom He wills” at 4:48 would be pointless.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16#2/r1.anchor: فلو كان كل من لم يشرك لم يعذب، لم يكن في قوله: { ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشآء } فائدة

QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.claim: An alternative contextual account identifies the giver as Abu al-Dahdah and the miser as the Ansari palm owner; it maps ease to Paradise, hardship to Hell, and death to loss of wealth.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.anchor: { فأما من أعطى واتقى } يعني أبا الدحداح. { وصدق بالحسنى } أي بالثواب

QUTB-ZILAL:92:16/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:92:16/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:92:16/r1.claim: The most wretched person is one who denies the call and turns away from guidance and the Lord's invitation to seek His promised guidance.
QUTB-ZILAL:92:16/r1.anchor: كذب بالدعوة وتولى عنها . تولى عن الهدى وعن دعوة ربه له ليهديه

RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r1.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r1.claim: The Qadi objects that other sinners would be excluded from Hell; Razi replies that every disbeliever denied the prophet and turned away from examining his signs, so all disbelievers fit the description.
RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r1.anchor: أن كل كافر لا بد وأن يكون مكذبا للنبي في دعواه

RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r2.claim: The claim that the verse encourages sin fails: present-world blame and God's withholding honor and reward can deter, and punishment may take other forms.
RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r2.anchor: يكفي في الزجر عن المعصية حصول الذم في العاجل

RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r5.claim: Reading 'most wretched' as merely more deserving of Hell abandons the apparent meaning without evidence.
RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r5.anchor: لأنه ترك للظاهر من غير دليل

SAMIN-DURR:92:15/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:92:15/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:92:15/r1.claim: One view takes ashqā and atqā to mean simply wretched and pious, without comparison, since the fire and its avoidance are not exclusive to the most extreme cases.
SAMIN-DURR:92:15/r1.anchor: قيل: الأشقى والأتقى بمعنى الشقي والتقي ولا تفضيل فيهما؛ لأن النار ليست مختصة بالأكثر شقاء

SAMIN-DURR:92:15/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:92:15/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:92:15/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī keeps the comparative force and explains the wording as a balance between an eminent unbeliever and believer, hyperbolically as if the fire and paradise were made for each alone; he identifies them as Abū Jahl or Umayya ibn Khalaf and Abū Bakr.
SAMIN-DURR:92:15/r2.anchor: الآية واردة في لموازنة بين حالتي عظيم من المشركين وعظيم من المؤمنين، فأريد أن يبالغ في صفتيهما

TAB:92:15/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:15/r1.speaker: author
TAB:92:15/r1.claim: Only the most wretched enters and burns in the Fire: the one who denied God's signs, turned away, and did not affirm them.
TAB:92:15/r1.anchor: لا يدخلها فيصلى بسعيرها إلاّ الأشقى ،   الذي كذّبَ وتَوَلّى يقول :  الذي كذّب بآيات ربه

TAB:92:15/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:15/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB:92:15/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra says all will enter Paradise except whoever refuses, and cites the description of the one who denied and turned away.
TAB:92:15/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة ،   قال :  لتدخُلنّ الجنة إلاّ من يأبى ،   قالوا :  يا أبا هريرة

TAB:92:15/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:15/r4.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB:92:15/r4.claim: Some Arab grammarians say takdhīb can mean failing in obedience: like a fighter who ‘lies’ by retreating, without an explicit denial.
TAB:92:15/r4.anchor: وكان بعض أهل العربية يقول :  لم يكن كذب بردّ ظاهر ،   ولكن قصّر عما أمر به

TAB:92:15/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:15/r5.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB:92:15/r5.claim: They cite an Arab expression meaning fighters did not retreat, and compare it with the Qur'anic description of the Event as having no falsehood.
TAB:92:15/r5.anchor: وذُكر أنه سمع بعض العرب يقول :  ليس لحدّهم مكذوبة ،   بمعنى :  أنهم إذا لقوا

TAB:92:16/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:16/r1.speaker: author
TAB:92:16/r1.claim: Only the most wretched enters and burns in the Fire: the one who denied God's signs, turned away, and did not affirm them.
TAB:92:16/r1.anchor: لا يدخلها فيصلى بسعيرها إلاّ الأشقى ،   الذي كذّبَ وتَوَلّى يقول :  الذي كذّب بآيات ربه

TAB:92:16/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:16/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB:92:16/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra says all will enter Paradise except whoever refuses, and cites the description of the one who denied and turned away.
TAB:92:16/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة ،   قال :  لتدخُلنّ الجنة إلاّ من يأبى ،   قالوا :  يا أبا هريرة

TAB:92:16/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:16/r3.speaker: الحسن
TAB:92:16/r3.claim: Al-Hasan identifies the most wretched as the polytheist; Muʿadh, rather than al-Hasan, adds ‘who denied and turned away.’
TAB:92:16/r3.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله :  لا يَصْلاها إلاّ الأشْقَى قال مُعاذ :  الذي كذّب وتولى

TAB:92:16/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:16/r4.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB:92:16/r4.claim: Some Arab grammarians say takdhīb can mean failing in obedience: like a fighter who ‘lies’ by retreating, without an explicit denial.
TAB:92:16/r4.anchor: وكان بعض أهل العربية يقول :  لم يكن كذب بردّ ظاهر ،   ولكن قصّر عما أمر به

TAB:92:16/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:16/r5.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB:92:16/r5.claim: They cite an Arab expression meaning fighters did not retreat, and compare it with the Qur'anic description of the Event as having no falsehood.
TAB:92:16/r5.anchor: وذُكر أنه سمع بعض العرب يقول :  ليس لحدّهم مكذوبة ،   بمعنى :  أنهم إذا لقوا

TAB-FULL:v24p476#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p476#3/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p476#3/r4.claim: Only the most wretched enters the blaze: the person who denied God's signs and turned away.
TAB-FULL:v24p476#3/r4.anchor: لا يدخلها فيصلى بسعيرها إلا الأشقى {الذي كذب وتولى} [الليل: 16]

TAB-FULL:v24p476#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p476#3/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB-FULL:v24p476#3/r5.claim: Abū Hurayra says everyone will enter Paradise except those who refuse, and identifies the refuser by the description of the one who denied and turned away.
TAB-FULL:v24p476#3/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، قال: لتدخلن الجنة إلا من يأبى، قالوا: يا أبا هريرة: ومن يأبى أن يدخل الجنة؟

TAB-FULL:v24p476#3/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p476#3/r7.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB-FULL:v24p476#3/r7.claim: Some grammarians say denial can figuratively mean falling short in obedience, like a warrior who retreats after meeting the enemy; they compare 56:2.
TAB-FULL:v24p476#3/r7.anchor: قصر عما أمر به من الطاعة، فجعل تكذيبا، كما تقول: لقي فلان العدو، فكذب إذا نكل ورجع

TABATABAI:92:13-16/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:13-16/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:92:13-16/r6.claim: Al-ashqā means any unbeliever who denies the true call and turns away, not the single most wretched person of all humanity; eternal afterlife misery exceeds temporary worldly suffering.
TABATABAI:92:13-16/r6.anchor: والمراد بالأشقى مطلق الكافر الذي يكفر بالتكذيب والتولي فإنه أشقى من سائر من شقي في دنياه

TABATABAI:92:13-16/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:13-16/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:92:13-16/r8.claim: The phrase “who denied and turned away” specifies the unbeliever’s defining response to the true call and supports the general reading of al-ashqā.
TABATABAI:92:13-16/r8.anchor: فالمراد بالأشقى هو الكافر المكذب بالدعوه الحقة المعرض عنها على ما يدل عليه توصيفه بقوله { الذي كذب وتولى }

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p87/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p87/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p87/r1.claim: The person described denied the Messenger and the Qurʾān and turned away from faith.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p87/r1.anchor: {الذي كذب} أي كذب الرسول، والقرآن (¬2). {وتولى} أعرض عن الإيمان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p87/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p87/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p87/r2.claim: The restriction to the denier applies to a particular level of Hell; its inhabitants occupy different levels.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p87/r2.anchor: أحدهما: أن هذا ورد في درك مخصوص من أدراك جهنم؛ لا يحله إلا) (¬4) من كان بهذه الصفة، وهي: دركات، ولأهل النار منها منازل، (وهذا قول أبي إسحاق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p87/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p87/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p87/r3.claim: Another answer is that mention of sinful non-polytheists is abbreviated; yuslīhā means enduring the fire's heat and does not itself imply abiding eternally, which only applies to the denying polytheist.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p87/r3.anchor: والثاني: أن هذا على الاختصار بحذف ذكر العصاة من غير المشركين، بدليل الآي الآخر، على أن معنى قوله: {لا يصلاها}

WAHIDI-QT:92:16/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:92:16/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:92:16/r1.claim: The wretched one is the person who denied and turned away.

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:16:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:16:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:16:anmerkung/r1.claim: The paired accusations of denial and turning away recur together in 96:13, 79:21–22, and 75:32; 88:23 substitutes kafara for kadhdhaba.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:16:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Die Vorwürfe des „Leugnens“ (des Jüngsten Gerichts) und „Abwendens“ werden auch

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:16:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:16:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:16:anmerkung/r2.claim: Kadhdhaba is central in early-Makkan preaching, appearing in punishment legends, their formulas, warnings, vice lists, and addresses to the condemned; early examples pair it with ‘Judgment.’
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:16:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Das Verb kaḏḏaba stellt eine der zentralen Begrifflichkeiten der frühmekkanischen Verkündigungen dar.

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:16:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:16:anmerkung/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:16:anmerkung/r3.claim: Because denial likely predates the Quranic usage, the term is not necessarily a Quranic coinage; its possible psalmic and especially Syriac kaddeb background includes lying, deception, treachery, and religious denial.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:16:anmerkung/r3.anchor: Als unmittelbarer Hintergrund des koranischen kaḏḏaba kommt jedoch am ehesten syr. kaddeb

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:14/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:14/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:14/r1.claim: Alongside showing people the right path, God warns through revelation and prophets against Hell, the consequence of following the wrong path.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:14/r1.anchor: yanlış yolda gitmenin sonucu olan cehenneme karşı da onları vahiy ve peygamberleri aracılığıyla uyarmıştır

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p382/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p382/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p382/r3.claim: Saying only the most pious will avoid the Fire would wrongly imply that other believers cannot be spared; God’s wording instead leaves His mercy open to them too.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p382/r3.anchor: وهذا من رحمة الله تعالى بعباده لأن معنى الآية أن الله تعالى يجنب الأتقى وغير الأتقى أيضاً

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p382/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p382/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p382/r5.claim: The opposite of the wretched is described at the highest level: the most pious gives his own wealth to purify himself, an image of maximal giving and sincerity.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p383/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p383/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p383/r1.claim: The earlier passage moves from particular acts toward a general description of evil; the good passage rises from giving to the highest piety and purification.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p383/r1.anchor: وفي الحسنة ترقى من الأفضل إلى الأفضل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p383/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p383/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p383/r2.claim: The passive verb signals that the pious person is spared by God, the creator of people and Fire, rather than escaping through his own power.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p383/r2.anchor: الله تعالى هو الذي يجنب عباده النار ولا أحد يستطيع أن يتجنبها بنفسه أبداً

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p383/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p383/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p383/r3.claim: People cannot save themselves from the Fire, even when they are the most pious and give their wealth in purification.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p383/r3.anchor: لا يستطيع الناس أن ينجوا بأنفسهم من النار ولو كان أحدهم الأتقى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p384/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p384/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p384/r1.claim: Deliverance may follow entry into harm and suffering, whereas sparing means being kept away before the harm is reached; the most pious is spared altogether.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p384/r1.anchor: التنجية قد تكون بعد الوقوع في الشيء ومعاناته

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p384/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p384/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p384/r2.claim: The Qur’an uses deliverance with those who are pious and sparing with the singular superlative, since the latter is kept from the trial itself.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p384/r2.anchor: مع اتقوا يستعمل القرآن لفظ (التنجية) ومع الأتقى يستعمل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#5/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#5/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#5/r1.claim: The unbeliever is the one who denied the truth and turned away from obedience.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#5/r1.anchor: الذي كذب أي بالحق وتولى وأعرض عن الطاعة

BINTSHATI:v2p114/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p114/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p114/r1.claim: The term ṣalā denotes roasting and punishment in blazing fire, rather than warmth sought for comfort.
BINTSHATI:v2p114/r1.anchor: وإنما هو الصلى بمعنى الشي والتعذيب باللهب المستعر في الجحيم.

BINTSHATI:v2p114/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p114/r2.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI:v2p114/r2.claim: Misery is the opposite of happiness and originally denotes hardship; al-Rāghib distinguishes it from mere fatigue, since every misery is toil but not every toil misery.
BINTSHATI:v2p114/r2.anchor: وهو ما نبه إليه "الراغب" بقوله في المفردات: كل شقاوة تعب، وليس كل تعب شقاوة.

BINTSHATI:v2p114/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p114/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p114/r3.claim: In Qur’anic usage, shaqāʾ chiefly names the ordeal of misguidance, explicitly in Ṭā Hā 123 and al-Muʾminūn 106 and by context in Hūd 105–106.
BINTSHATI:v2p114/r3.anchor: ويأتي الشقاء في الاستعمال القرآني خاصاً بمحنة الضلال، إما بصريح اللفظ

BINTSHATI:v2p114/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p114/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p114/r4.claim: Disobedience to God is close to misguidance as a sense of misery, as in the warning to Adam and Eve and the cited verses of Maryam.
BINTSHATI:v2p114/r4.anchor: وليس بعيداً من معنى الضلال، عصيان أمر الله، في قوله تعالى خطاباً لآدم وزوجه

BINTSHATI:v2p114/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p114/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p114/r5.claim: The construct form ashqāhā in the Thamūd account restricts the superlative to Thamūd: their most wretched, misguided, and transgressive member.
BINTSHATI:v2p114/r5.anchor: والإضافىة تقيده بالمضاف إليه، فهو أشقى ثمود وأضلها وأطغاها.

BINTSHATI:v2p114/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p114/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p114/r6.claim: Al-ashqā with the definite article occurs in al-Aʿlā and al-Layl in similar contexts; the source's following contrast is cut off in this segment.
BINTSHATI:v2p114/r6.anchor: والأشقى، معرفة بأل، في آيتى الأعلى والليل، والسياق فيهما متشابه

BURHAN:v4p90/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p90/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p90/r2.claim: In an adjective and similar constructions, agreement usually follows the preceding word’s form; agreement by meaning rather than form is rarer.
BURHAN:v4p90/r2.anchor: ثم الأكثر في نعتها وغيرها مرافقة اللفظ

ALUSI:92:16/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:16/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:16/r1.anchor: أي بالحق { وتولى } وأعرض عن الطاعة

ALUSI:92:16/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:16/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:16/r2.anchor: أي بالحق { وتولى } وأعرض عن الطاعة

BAGHAWI:92:16/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:16/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:92:16/r2.claim: The most wretched is the one who denied the Messenger and turned away from faith.
BAGHAWI:92:16/r2.anchor: الذي كذب } الرسول ،   { وتولى } عن الإيمان

BAYDAWI:92:16/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:92:16/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:92:16/r1.claim: The wretched one denied the truth and turned away from obedience.
BAYDAWI:92:16/r1.anchor: أي كذب الحق وأعرض عن الطاعة

BIQAI:92:16/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:16/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:92:16/r1.claim: The unbeliever corrupts his knowing faculty by denying what should be affirmed, and his acting faculty by arrogantly and stubbornly turning from truth, refusing to give wealth to purify himself.
BIQAI:92:16/r1.anchor: أفسد قوته العلمية بأن أوقع التكذيب بما حقه التصديق

DURR:92:15/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:15/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR:92:15/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra says people will enter Paradise except one who refuses; when asked who refuses Paradise, he recites the next verse about the one who denied and turned away.
DURR:92:15/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : لتدخلن الجنة إلا من يأبى . قالوا ومن يأبى أن يدخل الجنة ؟ فقرأ { الذي كذب وتولى }

DURR:92:15/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:15/r2.speaker: أبو أمامة
DURR:92:15/r2.claim: Abu Umama says everyone in this community will enter Paradise except one who strays from God like a bad camel from its master; he explains the wretched person as one who denied Muhammad's message and turned away.
DURR:92:15/r2.anchor: عن أبي أمامة قال : لا يبقى أحد من هذه الأمة إلا أدخله الله الجنة إلا من شرد على الله كما يشرد البعير السوء

DURR:92:16/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:16/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR:92:16/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra says people will enter Paradise except whoever refuses; when asked who refuses, he recites this verse’s description.
DURR:92:16/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : لتدخلن الجنة إلا من يأبى . قالوا ومن يأبى أن يدخل الجنة ؟ فقرأ

DURR:92:16/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:16/r2.speaker: أبو أمامة
DURR:92:16/r2.claim: Abu Umama says all the community enter Paradise except one who bolts from God like a bad camel; he explains the verse as rejecting Muhammad’s message and turning away.
DURR:92:16/r2.anchor: عن أبي أمامة قال : لا يبقى أحد من هذه الأمة إلا أدخله الله الجنة إلا من شرد على الله

DURR:92:16/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:16/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:92:16/r3.claim: The Prophet calls this the gentlest saying he heard: everyone enters Paradise except one who bolts away from God like a camel from its owner.
DURR:92:16/r3.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول : «كلكم يدخل الجنة إلا من شرد على الله شرد البعير على أهله

DURR:92:16/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:16/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:92:16/r4.claim: The Prophet says all his community enter Paradise except whoever refuses; refusing means disobeying him, while obeying him leads to Paradise.
DURR:92:16/r4.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «كل أمتي تدخل الجنة يوم القيامة إلا من أبى . قالوا : ومن يأبى يا رسول الله ؟

DURR:92:16/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:16/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:92:16/r5.claim: The Prophet says only a wretch enters Hell, defining the wretch as one who neither obeys God nor refrains from sin for His sake.
DURR:92:16/r5.anchor: عن أبي أمامة قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «لا يدخل النار إلا شقيّ . قيل : ومن الشقي ؟

IBNASHUR:92:15/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:15/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:15/r6.claim: The relative clause 'who denied and turned away' further specifies the intended people, who knew that they denied the Messenger and turned away from the Qurʾān.
IBNASHUR:92:15/r6.anchor: لزيادة التنصيص على أنهم المقصود بذلك فإنهم يعلمون أنهم كذبوا الرسول

IBNASHUR:92:15/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:15/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:15/r10.claim: The relative clauses describing the most wretched and most pious signal that their respective actions cause the stated outcome.
IBNASHUR:92:15/r10.anchor: للإيذان بأن للصلة تسببا في الحكم

IBNATIYYA:92:16/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:92:16/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:92:16/r3.claim: The description of denial identifies the ashqā of the preceding verse as an unbeliever.
IBNATIYYA:92:16/r3.anchor: و { الأشقى } هنا ،   الكافر بدليل قوله الذي كذب

IBNATIYYA:92:16/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:92:16/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:92:16/r4.claim: He cites Ṭarafa's awḥad as evidence that Arabs use an afʿal form for fāʿil emphatically.
IBNATIYYA:92:16/r4.anchor: والعرب تجعل أفعل في موضع فاعل مبالغة كما قال طرفة : [ الطويل ] تمنى رجال أن أموت

IBNKATHIR:92:16/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:92:16/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:92:16/r1.claim: The person denies with his heart and turns away by refusing action through his limbs and bodily faculties.
IBNKATHIR:92:16/r1.anchor: أي : بقلبه ،   { وَتَوَلَّى } أي : عن العمل بجوارحه وأركانه

IBNKATHIR:92:16/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:92:16/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:92:16/r2.claim: The Prophet says only a wretched person enters the Fire, defining that person as one who neither obeys God nor leaves a sin for His sake.
IBNKATHIR:92:16/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : " لا يدخل النار إلا شقي " . قيل : ومن الشقي ؟ قال : " الذي لا يعمل بطاعة ،   ولا يترك لله معصية "

IBNKATHIR:92:16/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:92:16/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:92:16/r3.claim: The Prophet says his community will enter Paradise except those who refuse: whoever obeys him enters it, and whoever disobeys has refused.
IBNKATHIR:92:16/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : " كل أمتي تدخل الجنة يوم القيامة إلا من أبى "

MAWARDI:92:16/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:16/r1.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI:92:16/r1.claim: Qatāda says he denied God's Book and turned away from obedience to God.
MAWARDI:92:16/r1.anchor: أحدهما : كذب بكتاب الله وتولى عن طاعة الله ،   قاله قتادة

MAWARDI:92:16/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:16/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI:92:16/r2.claim: Another interpretation is that he denied the Messenger and turned away from obeying him.

NASAFI:92:16/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:92:16/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:92:16/r1.claim: The most wretched is the unbeliever who denied the messengers and turned away from faith.
NASAFI:92:16/r1.anchor: إلا الكافر الذي كذب الرسل وأعرض عن الإيمان

QURTUBI:92:16/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:16/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:92:16/r1.claim: The one who denied is the Prophet Muhammad's message, and turning away means turning away from faith.
QURTUBI:92:16/r1.anchor: " الذي كذب " نبي اللّه محمدا صلى اللّه عليه وسلم . " وتولى " أي أعرض عن الإيمان

QURTUBI:92:16/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:16/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI:92:16/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that everyone enters Paradise except whoever refuses it; he identifies the refuser as the one who denied and turned away.
QURTUBI:92:16/r2.anchor: وروى مكحول عن أبي هريرة قال : كل يدخل الجنة إلا من أباها

QURTUBI:92:16/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:16/r3.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI:92:16/r3.claim: Malik recounts Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz crying so hard at the warning of blazing Fire during Maghrib prayer that he could not continue the sura and read another.
QURTUBI:92:16/r3.anchor: وقال مالك : صلى بنا عمر بن عبد العزيز المغرب ، فقرأ " والليل إذا يغشى "

QURTUBI:92:16/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:16/r4.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI:92:16/r4.claim: Al-Farra says the wretched one is whoever was wretched in God's knowledge.
QURTUBI:92:16/r4.anchor: إلا من كان شقيا في علم اللّه جل ثناؤه

QURTUBI:92:16/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:16/r5.speaker: ابن عباس عن الضحاك
QURTUBI:92:16/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas, through al-Dahhak, identifies the wretched one with Umayya ibn Khalaf and those like him who denied Muhammad.
QURTUBI:92:16/r5.anchor: وروى الضحاك عن ابن عباس قال : " لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى " أمية بن خلف ونظراؤه

QURTUBI:92:16/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:16/r6.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI:92:16/r6.claim: Qatada says he denied God's Book and turned away from obedience to God.
QURTUBI:92:16/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة : كذب بكتاب اللّه ، وتولى عن طاعة اللّه

QURTUBI:92:16/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:16/r7.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI:92:16/r7.claim: Al-Farra says this need not mean explicit denial: falling short of commanded obedience is called denial, like facing an enemy and then retreating.
QURTUBI:92:16/r7.anchor: وقال الفراء : لم يكن كذب برد ظاهر ، ولكنه قصر عما أمر به من الطاعة ، فجعل تكذيبا

QURTUBI:92:16/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:16/r8.speaker: أبو ثروان
QURTUBI:92:16/r8.claim: Abu Tharwan's idiom about Banu Numayr says their forebear has no retreat in him, meaning they fight truthfully and do not turn back.
QURTUBI:92:16/r8.anchor: وسمعت أبا ثروان يقول : إن بني نمير

QURTUBI:92:16/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:16/r9.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI:92:16/r9.claim: Al-Farra connects the same usage to the verse saying the Hour's arrival has no falsehood, meaning it is certainly true.
QURTUBI:92:16/r9.anchor: وكذلك قوله جل ثناؤه :  " ليس لوقعتها

QURTUBI:92:16/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:16/r10.speaker: أبو إسحاق الزجاج
QURTUBI:92:16/r10.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the Murji'a use these verses to argue that only unbelievers enter the Fire.

QURTUBI:92:16/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:16/r11.speaker: أبو إسحاق الزجاج
QURTUBI:92:16/r11.claim: Al-Zajjaj rejects that inference: this is a particular Fire, while Hell has levels, including the hypocrites' lowest level, and God may punish with any threatened kind of torment.

QURTUBI:92:16/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:16/r12.speaker: أبو إسحاق الزجاج
QURTUBI:92:16/r12.claim: Al-Zajjaj adds that God forgives sins short of associating partners for whomever He wills; otherwise that promise would have no meaning, so non-polytheists may still be punished.
QURTUBI:92:16/r12.anchor: وقال جل ثناؤه :  " إن الله لا يغفر أن يشرك به

RAZI:92:15/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:15/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI:92:15/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the passage was revealed about Umayya ibn Khalaf and others who denied Muhammad and earlier prophets.
RAZI:92:15/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس : نزلت في أمية بن خلف وأمثاله الذين كذبوا محمدا والأنبياء قبله

RAZI:92:15/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:15/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:92:15/r2.claim: Al-Razi says al-ashqā can mean “wretched,” as in “not the one-and-only”; he explains the phrase as a disbeliever who rejects God's signs and turns from obedience.
RAZI:92:15/r2.anchor: وقيل : إن الأشقى بمعنى الشقي كما يقال : لست فيها بأوحد أي بواحد

RAZI:92:15/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:15/r3.speaker: المرجئة
RAZI:92:15/r3.claim: The Murjiʾites use the passage to argue only unbelievers are threatened with punishment.
RAZI:92:15/r3.anchor: واعلم أن المرجئة يتمسكون بهذه الآية في أنه لا وعيد إلا على الكفار

RAZI:92:15/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:15/r4.speaker: القاضي
RAZI:92:15/r4.claim: Al-Qāḍī argues that the apparent restriction would keep from Hell an unbeliever who had not denied and turned away.
RAZI:92:15/r4.anchor: قال القاضي : ولا يمكن إجراء هذه الآية على ظاهرها ، ويدل على ذلك ثلاثة أوجه ( أحدها ) : أنه يقتضي أن لا يدخل النار

RAZI:92:15/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:15/r5.speaker: القاضي
RAZI:92:15/r5.claim: Al-Qāḍī argues the restriction invites sin by assuring believers who did not deny or turn away that sin cannot harm them, virtually permitting it.
RAZI:92:15/r5.anchor: ( وثانيها ) : أن هذا إغراء بالمعاصي ، لأنه بمنزلة أن يقول الله تعالى : لمن صدق بالله ورسوله ولم يكذب ولم يتول

RAZI:92:15/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:15/r9.speaker: author
RAZI:92:15/r9.claim: Al-Razi replies that every unbeliever denies the prophet's claim and turns away from examining its proofs, so all unbelievers fit the description.
RAZI:92:15/r9.anchor: أن كل كافر لابد وأن يكون مكذبا للنبي في دعواه ، ويكون متوليا عن النظر في دلالة صدق ذلك النبي

RAZI:92:15/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:15/r10.speaker: author
RAZI:92:15/r10.claim: Al-Razi rejects the charge of enticing sin: present disgrace and God's anger deter, and God may punish another way; punishment need not be limited to Hell.
RAZI:92:15/r10.anchor: لأنه يكفي في الزجر عن المعصية حصول الذم في العاجل وحصول غضب الله

RAZI:92:16/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:16/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI:92:16/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the passage was revealed about Umayya ibn Khalaf and others who denied Muhammad and earlier prophets.
RAZI:92:16/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس : نزلت في أمية بن خلف وأمثاله الذين كذبوا محمدا والأنبياء قبله

RAZI:92:16/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:16/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:92:16/r2.claim: Al-Razi says al-ashqā can mean “wretched,” as in “not the one-and-only”; he explains the phrase as a disbeliever who rejects God's signs and turns from obedience.
RAZI:92:16/r2.anchor: وقيل : إن الأشقى بمعنى الشقي كما يقال : لست فيها بأوحد أي بواحد

RAZI:92:16/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:16/r3.speaker: المرجئة
RAZI:92:16/r3.claim: The Murjiʾites use the passage to argue only unbelievers are threatened with punishment.
RAZI:92:16/r3.anchor: واعلم أن المرجئة يتمسكون بهذه الآية في أنه لا وعيد إلا على الكفار

RAZI:92:16/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:16/r4.speaker: القاضي
RAZI:92:16/r4.claim: Al-Qāḍī argues that the apparent restriction would keep from Hell an unbeliever who had not denied and turned away.
RAZI:92:16/r4.anchor: قال القاضي : ولا يمكن إجراء هذه الآية على ظاهرها ، ويدل على ذلك ثلاثة أوجه ( أحدها ) : أنه يقتضي أن لا يدخل النار

RAZI:92:16/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:16/r5.speaker: القاضي
RAZI:92:16/r5.claim: Al-Qāḍī argues the restriction invites sin by assuring believers who did not deny or turn away that sin cannot harm them, virtually permitting it.
RAZI:92:16/r5.anchor: ( وثانيها ) : أن هذا إغراء بالمعاصي ، لأنه بمنزلة أن يقول الله تعالى : لمن صدق بالله ورسوله ولم يكذب ولم يتول

RAZI:92:16/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:16/r9.speaker: author
RAZI:92:16/r9.claim: Al-Razi replies that every unbeliever denies the prophet's claim and turns away from examining its proofs, so all unbelievers fit the description.
RAZI:92:16/r9.anchor: أن كل كافر لابد وأن يكون مكذبا للنبي في دعواه ، ويكون متوليا عن النظر في دلالة صدق ذلك النبي

RAZI:92:16/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:16/r10.speaker: author
RAZI:92:16/r10.claim: Al-Razi rejects the charge of enticing sin: present disgrace and God's anger deter, and God may punish another way; punishment need not be limited to Hell.
RAZI:92:16/r10.anchor: لأنه يكفي في الزجر عن المعصية حصول الذم في العاجل وحصول غضب الله

QURTUBI:92:20/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:20/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI:92:20/r17.claim: The miser's wealth cannot help at death; the one who enters the fire is the hypocritical Khazrajī, who died in hypocrisy, while Abū al-Daḥdāḥ is kept from it.
QURTUBI:92:20/r17.anchor: أي مات . إلى قوله : " لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى " يعني بذلك الخزرجي
